turns.t: Good afternoon. Before we start, what shall I call you, Mr Subramaniam, or Raghu, or sir? ~
Raghu is fine, everyone calls me that. I was a schoolteacher, you know, forty years, and they still call me Sir at the vegetable shop.
Sir it is, then, in the vegetable shop. And this is? ~
I'm Sunita, I stay with him as his carer. I'm here because the evenings are very difficult now.
Tell me about the evenings.
He gets confused. After the lights come on he asks me where his wife is, and she passed ten years ago. It started about three months ago, I'd say.
No, no, it's not three months. It began last month, one month, maybe, when the clocks changed.
One month, or three months. We'll note somewhere between one and three months. And what happens during the confusion, Raghu?
I get a bit muddled. It's the television, it confuses me. ~
Is he restless too, Sunita?
Yes, in the evenings he paces. Up and down the corridor, it takes an hour to settle him.
Any falls?
No falls. I am a very steady man.
Sir, you fell in the bathroom two weeks ago. I helped you up.
That was a slip, it was nothing.
I'll record that Sunita saw a fall and you say it didn't happen. Any fever or cold symptoms recently?
None of that.
What medicines is he taking, Sunita?
Amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day. Donepezil, 5 mg, at night. And tamsulosin, 400 micrograms, after dinner.
And any allergies to medicines, Raghu?
No, I have no allergies. None.
Sir, the antibiotic you had at the hospital last year, you were so itchy. I don't know which one it was.
I don't remember any itching.
I'll keep both. Health problems, Raghu?
High blood pressure, and the prostate, it's enlarged.
Any operations?
Cataract, both eyes, two years ago. Very good surgeon.
Who is at home with you?
I live in with him, his son visits at the weekends.
Raghu, can you tell me today's date? ~
It's... Tuesday? No, I'm not sure. Sunita will know. ~
Do you know where we are?
A hospital. No, the clinic, the doctor's clinic. I know it very well, I come here every year.
He knows his name and the place but not the date. Now stand up and walk to the door for me.
Slowly, sir, take your stick. ~
He walks slowly with a stick, but he's steady enough.
I told you, steady. ~
Any trouble passing water, Raghu?
No, nothing now, the tablet helps.
What I think is happening is evening confusion, what we call sundowning, and I'd like to rule out other causes.
Is it serious, doctor? ~
It's common at his age. I'd like to arrange blood tests to rule out infection and vitamin problems.
When should I bring him? ~
The blood test is at the front desk, this week. Keep the house bright in the evenings, close the curtains before dark, and keep the television off.
I'll do that. ~
I'd like to see you again in two weeks, and Sunita, write down what happens each evening.
Two weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
